Current allocation: View A is focused on the upper location (selection ≈ 0.9995). The model represents that upper object as green and almost certainly square (recoverability now/1/2 steps ≈ 0.700, 0.502, 0.363). View B is focused on the left location (selection ≈ 0.99997); that object is represented as red circle (recoverability ≈ 0.680, 0.484, 0.343).

Other remembered items (less likely to be selected): In A, right = red cross (very low selection; recoverability ≈ 0.568, 0.415, 0.292); left = blue circle (very low selection; recoverability ≈ 0.216, 0.161, 0.121); lower = completely uncertain color/shape (very low selection; recoverability ≈ 0.033, 0.036, 0.033). In B, upper = green triangle (very low selection; recoverability ≈ 0.508, 0.370, 0.267); right = yellow square (very low selection; recoverability ≈ 0.102, 0.088, 0.068); lower = blue with cross bias (very low selection; recoverability ≈ 0.163, 0.124, 0.098).

How redirection would change selection: In View B, commands reliably switch selection to the commanded location (upper→upper, right→right, lower→lower, left→left; each ≈ 0.999 on its target), so B is under strong control. In View A, commands do not select the commanded locations; instead the model predicts selection will almost certainly move to the lower location regardless of which command is issued (predicted next selection for lower ≈ 0.998–0.999), so A is not under effective command control.
